title: The Voyage to Punt
objective: After this level you can describe Egypt's trade expeditions to the land of Punt.
summary: Egypt sailed the Red Sea to Punt for incense, gold, leopard skins and baboons, carrying ships across the desert. Punt’s location is still debated.

cards.headline: Egypt sailed to a land of incense and gold. Nobody knows exactly where.
cards.body: Egyptians called it Punt, and they went to remarkable lengths to get there.

cards.headline: The wonders of Punt
cards.body: From Punt, Egyptian expeditions brought back incense, gold, leopard skins and even living baboons. Voyages there are recorded at least as early as about 2200 BCE, under Pepi II. The most famous one, sent by Hatshepsut, was carved on the walls of her temple at Deir el-Bahri. It was a shopping trip worth writing on a temple.

cards.headline: Flat-pack ships
cards.body: Getting there took ingenuity. At Wadi Gawasis on the Red Sea coast, archaeologists found that Egyptians built ships by the Nile, took them apart, carried them across the desert and put them back together on the shore. Caves there held ship timbers, rope and cargo boxes labeled “wonders of Punt,” from roughly 4,000 years ago. Flat-pack furniture, but make it a seagoing ship.

cards.headline: So where was it?
cards.body: Punt lay somewhere around the southern Red Sea, and scholars have argued over it for more than 150 years. The leading candidates include the Horn of Africa and southern Arabia. One clue came from baboon mummies: chemical signatures in two New Kingdom baboons point to Eritrea, Ethiopia or Somalia. The researchers call the result provisional.
cards.callout: Horn of Africa or southern Arabia? Still debated

questions.prompt: What did Egyptian expeditions bring back from Punt?

options.label: Incense, gold, leopard skins and living baboons
Grain to feed Egypt in famine years

questions.explanation: Punt supplied incense, gold, leopard skins and live baboons.

questions.prompt: How did mummified baboons help the search for Punt?

options.label: Their wrappings were labeled with Punt’s location
options.rationale: The clue was chemical, not written.

options.label: They were buried with maps of the Red Sea
Their species lives only in Arabia
options.rationale: The clue came from their chemistry.

options.label: Chemical signatures in them hint at where the animals came from

questions.explanation: Isotope signatures in two New Kingdom baboons point to Eritrea, Ethiopia or Somalia, though the result is provisional.

questions.prompt: The Nile was Egypt’s main road (Level 5). Why did voyages to Punt need more than the river?

options.label: The Nile was closed to royal ships
options.rationale: The river was Egypt’s great highway.

options.label: Punt lay on the Red Sea, so ships were carried overland to the coast
The Nile flowed the wrong way for trade
options.rationale: Egyptians used both current and wind.

options.label: Punt was reached by camel caravan only

questions.explanation: The Nile could not reach the Red Sea, so ships were built by the river, carried across the desert and rebuilt on the coast.
